objective: Add a local Cloud IaC app entrypoint and binary metadata that wires /healthz, /livez, and the OpenTofu module-registry routes through the canonical Hyper adapter, including bounded loopback daemon evidence and Helm cargoPackage alignment, without claiming deployment, production authentication, persistence, provider runtime, OpenTofu plan/apply, FD-001 tenant workload hosting, or cloud provisioning.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu discovery starts at /.well-known/terraform.json and returns service identifiers such as modules.v1.
Module registry versions and download endpoints are GET routes under the discovered modules.v1 base path.
Registry module sources are distinct from provider execution, credentials, state backend, and plan/apply concerns.

implemented_claims: Added oya-cloud-iac-app package with library and oya-cloud-iac binary metadata as the local Cloud IaC composition root.
Added /healthz and /livez handlers plus existing OpenTofu module-registry routes in one canonical Router<SyncHandler> service.
Added bounded Cloud IaC app loopback serving evidence over real HTTP/1.1 through the Hyper adapter for two requests.

Added Hyper adapter serve_listener, serve_n_connections, serve_n_connections_on_std_listener, and serve_on_std_listener so downstream crates can run daemon/bounded harnesses without declaring tokio or hyper.
Aligned Helm values microservice.cargoPackage with the new oya-cloud-iac-app package while leaving deployment rollout as a nonclaim.
Updated manifest, catalog, tasks, evidence, and audit chain with truthful local app-entrypoint scope.
explicit_non_claims: no production authentication runtime or Cedar runtime integration
no persistence, database adapter, or object-store module serving
no signed module releases, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD rollout, Kubernetes rollout, or Jenkins pipeline execution
no measured SLO, DR, sharding execution, tenant migration, or capacity telemetry
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant evidence
no aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all success claim for current worktree
false_green_findings_closed: Helm values referenced a Cloud IaC cargo package but no app entrypoint package existed; oya-cloud-iac-app now exists and Helm cargoPackage names it.
Previous one-connection evidence proved only a single registry request; bounded app loopback evidence now proves the app router can serve health and OpenTofu discovery through the same Hyper seam.
Tokio remains isolated in the Hyper adapter; the app entrypoint uses blocking adapter wrappers instead of adding direct tokio/hyper dependencies.

Initial app catalog role as app violated architecture-boundaries for app -> api/runtime edges; catalog role was corrected to runtime composition-root so the dependency edge gate passes without weakening the gate.
known_gaps: Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed; repo-wide unrelated blockers remain outside this Cloud IaC slice.
Aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all is not claimed green unless freshly re-run and proven.
Default app startup currently uses an empty in-memory module registry; loading release-index/archive metadata into the app is a future ChangeSet.
Production request authentication, persistence, module object storage, signed releases, OpenTofu plan/apply, provider runtime, and live GitOps/Kubernetes rollout evidence remain future work.
FD-001 remains the product delivery goal; this ChangeSet is substrate progress only and does not prove FD-001 tenant workload hosting.

findings: Kept the implementation boring: a small composition-root crate, two fixed health routes, and adapter-local listener wrappers instead of a new HTTP stack or framework.
Moves Cloud IaC from library-only loopback evidence toward a runnable control-plane process seam while preserving honest nonclaims for production readiness and tenant workload hosting.
RED proved the app package was absent. GREEN sends two raw HTTP/1.1 loopback requests through the app service and asserts health/discovery responses.
The app crate exposes config parsing, service construction, bounded serving for tests, and indefinite serving for the binary entrypoint without leaking async runtime dependencies.
Focused tests, scoped tests, fmt/check/clippy, catalog, architecture, api, planning, and Cloud IaC regression gates passed; run-all/full verify remain transparently unclaimed.

alternatives_named: Add tokio to the app crate

rejected_reasons: Direct tokio app dependency would violate current seam policy.
Library-only loopback would leave Helm/app entrypoint mismatch unclosed.
